outcome: Incidence of specific etiologies of respiratory distress (respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn, meconium aspiration syndrome, pneumonia)
Severity of respiratory distress (Downe's and Silverman-Anderson scores)
cohort: The study included 250 neonates admitted to a tertiary care NICU with respiratory distress.
finding: The most common etiologies of respiratory distress were respiratory distress syndrome (32.8%), transient tachypnea of the newborn (27.2%), meconium aspiration syndrome (14.8%), and pneumonia (18%), with preterm neonates exhibiting a higher incidence of RDS and term neonates showing a predominance of TTN and MAS.
